description:
FILED by the s532 Fable merge review (2026-11-02), probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s532/review/merge-review/probes/e1688-3.pl (needs PCL_REVIEW_PROBES=.../probes for its `use lib`).  PRE-EXISTING: base d47caabe and main b31345ca identical.  Found while probing #1688 (require answers the file's value) -- the bare spellings `my $again = require A;` and `eval "require $m"` are right on main.

    use lib "...";
    print "v: ", (require A), "\n";
    # perl: "v: 1"
    # PCL:  PCL: statement not supported at ... line 3: print "v: ", (require A), "\n"; -- Handle single node of unknown type. Dump: ...   exit 2

MECHANISM (likely): the Statement::Include special-casing lives at statement level (Pl::Parser::_process_include_statement); a `require` Word inside a PPI::Structure::List reaches PExpr as a plain Word + a bareword argument, which the term walker declines (the "single node of unknown type" drop).  FIX SHAPE: PExpr lowers `require BAREWORD` / `require EXPR` in expression position the way the statement form does (ONE lowering, rule 11: the include statement's require arm becomes the expression form's caller), with #1688's value semantics; guard rows in Pl/t/use-require-01.t (`my @x = (1, (require A), 2)`, the print shape).  LOW: a rare spelling; no board row known behind it.


=== DONE (s532b) ===
FIXED (Pl/PExpr.pm): PPI classes a statement by its first token, so the parenthesised run `(require A)` is a PPI::Statement::Include child of the Structure::List (dumped), while `my $v = require A` is plain tokens; parse()'s single-statement unwrap now accepts a Statement::Include whose type is `require` beside Statement / Expression / Break / Variable -- the same term once unwrapped.  Probed = perl: the print shape, `(1, (require A), 2)`, `my $s = (require A)`, `... if (require A)`, `map { (require A) }`, `(require "$m.pm")` in an eval, two in a join list.  Not a PPI bug for the catalogue: the statement class by first token is PPI's design (an Include inside a List is still an include).  Guard Pl/t/use-require-01.t last row.


=== COMPLETED (s535, reviewing session): merged in MAIN-READY-71 4748a7f5 (s532b); review probes perl -> main -> tree identical. ===
subject: A parenthesised `(require NAME)` inside a list -- `print "v: ", (require A), "\n";` -- is a statement drop ("Handle single node of unknown type"); `my $v = require A;` and `eval "require $m"` work
